question: Which pair of findings best explains why average scores sit below 50% even when many formulas look right?
options: Models pass most perturbation checks but far fewer formula checks, since they rarely recalculate
Models pass most output-validation checks but far fewer static formula and presentation checks
Models pass most checks on manipulation but far fewer on synthesis, which pulls averages down
Models pass most static formula checks but far fewer output-validation and perturbation checks

private.explanation: The sharpest finding is the static-versus-dynamic gap, which the summed score hides.
option_explanations: Perturbation had the lowest pass rates (15-37%), and recalculation was common among stronger models.
Output Validation pass rates (20-48%) were lower than Formula Correctness (50-68%), not higher.
Manipulation scores were lower than synthesis, so this reverses the finding.
Correct: a roughly 30-point gap separates static from dynamic criteria.
